segments.t: Font, color and cursor overrides for the Snippet Manager and the Snippet Edit dialog, plus how many Full code analyses korTTY keeps per snippet and how large a script's text may be to be stored with them. Open via KTPH001Configuration → Global Settings → Snippet EditorKTPH002; stored in KTPH000.
Empty (inherit) or an installed monospace family
One key, optionally with up to three modifiers (Ctrl/Cmd, Shift, Alt)
Off, 256 KB, 512 KB, 1 MB, 2 MB, 5 MB

Click the KTPH022AI Completion ShortcutKTPH023 field and press the combination you want — the field records what you pressed, and KTPH024ResetKTPH025 restores KTPH026KTPH000KTPH027+KTPH028KTPH001KTPH029. A combination is one main key (a letter, digit, function key, KTPH030KTPH002KTPH031, KTPH032KTPH003KTPH033, an arrow, KTPH034KTPH004KTPH035 and so on) with none, one, two or three modifiers, so KTPH036KTPH005KTPH037 alone, KTPH038KTPH006KTPH039+KTPH040KTPH007KTPH041 and KTPH042KTPH008KTPH043+KTPH044KTPH009KTPH045+KTPH046KTPH010KTPH047 are all valid. On macOS the KTPH048KTPH011KTPH049 modifier is the Cmd key, matching the editor's own shortcuts. The new combination applies to snippet editors opened afterwards; KTPH050KTPH012KTPH051+KTPH052KTPH013KTPH053 opens the list as well and cannot be reassigned. Choosing something other than KTPH054KTPH014KTPH055+KTPH056KTPH015KTPH057 gives KTPH058KTPH016KTPH059+KTPH060KTPH017KTPH061 back its normal editor meaning: it removes one level of indentation. A Snippet Manager open as a tab of the main window cannot use KTPH062KTPH018KTPH063+KTPH064KTPH019KTPH065 to KTPH066KTPH020KTPH067+KTPH068KTPH021KTPH069, because those keys KTPH070jump to a tabKTPH071 there; a Snippet Manager window of its own can.

With KTPH000Keep a pre-warmed editor readyKTPH001 on, korTTY boots a spare editor in the background about two seconds after the first snippet editor of a session has opened, so the next Snippet Edit dialog or Snippet Manager preview starts with a ready editor instead of loading Monaco while you wait. The spare is only created after you have used an editor once, and it holds a WebKit page in memory while idle — switch the option off on machines with little RAM to trade a short boot per open for that memory.

How many KTPH000Full code analysesKTPH001 korTTY keeps for each snippet. When a new analysis of a snippet arrives and its history is over the limit, the oldest analyses are removed; pinned analyses, analyses with a result waiting for review and analyses with an interrupted apply are always kept, so a history can hold more than the limit. Lowering the value deletes nothing right away: the settings tab says how many older, unpinned analyses the next analysis of each snippet would remove, and they only go when that analysis arrives. To remove analyses now, use KTPH002DiscardKTPH003 or KTPH004Delete allKTPH005 in the analysis panel.

The largest script text — measured in bytes of UTF-8 — that korTTY stores with a KTPH001Full code analysisKTPH002. Every analysis can hold several copies of the script (the analysed text, the text an apply started from, the proposed result and the accepted text); each copy up to this size is stored completely, identical copies only once. The default is KTPH0031 MBKTPH004, the maximum is KTPH0055 MBKTPH006, and KTPH007OffKTPH008 stores no script text at all — findings, the diagram and the reports stay. A larger script is still analysed and can still be applied and reviewed in the editor; only its stored copies are missing afterwards, so KTPH009View changesKTPH010, the code preview of an older entry, the plain-text script export, the report appendix, KTPH011Restore intermediate stateKTPH012 and resuming an interrupted apply after a restart are not available for it, and the panel says why. Lowering the value deletes nothing: text that is already stored stays, and the new limit applies to analyses made from then on. A larger value uses more disk space in KTPH000; a file that would grow beyond 60 MB sheds the stored text of the oldest analyses first. An administrator can cap the value or forbid storing script text with the KTPH013enterprise policyKTPH014; the dropdown then only offers what the policy allows, says so beneath it and is locked when the policy forbids storing script text.

These settings override the terminal/editor defaults for snippet windows only. Leave a field empty — or set the font size to KTPH000 — to inherit the general setting from KTPH001AppearanceKTPH002, KTPH003ColorsKTPH004 and KTPH005EditorKTPH006 instead.
The snippet editor itself, including its AI code actions and language fields, is described under KTPH000SnippetsKTPH001.
